purpose: Control the systemd service manager. The primary interface for managing units (start, stop, enable, disable, status, list) and the system (reboot, poweroff, isolate). Talks to PID 1 via D-Bus.

flags.name: status [UNIT]
flags.doc: Show unit status + recent log lines. Without arg = systemd manager status.

flags.name: enable UNIT
flags.doc: Create symlinks per [Install] section so unit starts at boot.

flags.name: enable --now UNIT
flags.doc: Enable AND start in one shot.

flags.name: mask UNIT
flags.doc: Symlink unit to /dev/null — prevents any start (manual or dep-pulled).

flags.name: reset-failed [UNIT]
flags.doc: Clear 'failed' state so the unit can restart again.

flags.name: daemon-reload
flags.doc: Re-read unit files after editing on disk.

flags.name: list-sockets
flags.doc: List socket units + their listening addrs.

flags.name: edit --full UNIT
flags.doc: Edit entire unit file (copies vendor unit to /etc/systemd/system/).

flags.name: set-property UNIT KEY=VAL
flags.doc: Runtime + persistent property update (e.g. systemctl set-property foo.service MemoryMax=2G).

flags.name: isolate TARGET
flags.doc: Switch active target (like SysV runlevel change). Stops conflicting units.

flags.name: --user
flags.doc: Operate on per-user systemd instance instead of system.

flags.name: --no-block
flags.doc: Don't wait for command to complete (return immediately).

flags.name: --lines=N
flags.doc: Number of journal lines in status output (default 10).

examples.expected_output: unit state, PID, recent journal lines
examples.scenario: Universal 'how is X doing?' command.
Triage: what broke?

examples.invocation: systemctl edit --full myapp.service && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart myapp
examples.scenario: Edit-then-reload pattern for changing service config.

purpose: Query systemd journal logs. The replacement for grep'ing /var/log/syslog. Filter by unit, priority, time, fields. Tail with -f.

flags.name: -p PRIORITY
flags.doc: Max priority (0-7 or name: emerg/alert/crit/err/warning/notice/info/debug). e.g. -p err shows ≤ err.

flags.name: -b [BOOT]
flags.doc: Current boot only. -b -1 = previous boot. journalctl --list-boots lists.

flags.name: -S, --since TIME
flags.doc: Since time. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or 'yesterday' or '1 hour ago' or '-1h'.

flags.name: -n N, --lines=N
flags.doc: Last N lines (default 10 with -f, all without).

flags.name: -o FORMAT
flags.doc: Output format: short (default), short-iso, short-precise, short-monotonic, verbose, export, json, json-pretty, cat (just MESSAGE), with-unit.

flags.name: -x, --catalog
flags.doc: Show extended explanations (the catalog) for known events.

flags.name: FIELD=VALUE
flags.doc: Match by field. e.g. _PID=1234, _UID=1000, _SYSTEMD_UNIT=foo.service. Multiple = AND. + separates OR groups.

flags.name: --list-boots
flags.doc: List boots with offset, ID, time range.

flags.name: --vacuum-size=SIZE
flags.doc: Reduce disk to SIZE (delete oldest archived journals).

flags.name: --vacuum-files=N
flags.doc: Keep at most N archive files.

flags.name: --show-cursor
flags.doc: Print cursor of last entry shown (for next --cursor).

examples.scenario: Watch a service's logs in real time.
Find recent errors after a problem.
Structured filter for log analysis.

purpose: Inspect boot performance, unit-file correctness, sandboxing posture. The performance + correctness toolbox.

flags.name: blame
flags.doc: Per-unit time-to-active sorted by slowest. The 'who's slowing my boot' query.

flags.name: critical-chain [UNIT]
flags.doc: Tree of units on the critical path.

flags.name: plot > boot.svg
flags.doc: SVG timeline of boot. Visual gold.

flags.name: dump
flags.doc: Full state dump of every unit (huge).

flags.name: verify UNIT
flags.doc: Lint unit files for syntax + reference errors.

flags.name: security UNIT
flags.doc: Audit a service's sandboxing — assigns a security score (0-10, 0 = best). Lists missing hardening directives.

flags.name: cat-config FILE
flags.doc: Show config + drop-ins for a config file.

flags.name: calendar 'EXPR'
flags.doc: Show next firing time for an OnCalendar= expression.

examples.scenario: Diagnose slow boots.
Audit a service's sandbox posture.
Validate a unit file before applying.

purpose: Run a command as a transient unit (service, scope, or timer). Lets you apply systemd resource controls + sandboxing to ad-hoc invocations.

flags.name: -u, --unit=NAME
flags.doc: Name for the transient unit. Default = systemd-generated.

flags.name: --scope
flags.doc: Run as scope (vs default service). Useful when calling systemd-run interactively — your shell becomes the scope's process.

flags.name: --slice=SLICE
flags.doc: Place under SLICE (defaults to system.slice or user.slice).

flags.name: -p PROP=VAL
flags.doc: Set unit property. e.g. -p MemoryMax=2G -p CPUQuota=50%. Multiple -p allowed.

flags.name: -G, --collect
flags.doc: Auto-collect (clean up failed unit) on exit.

flags.name: --wait
flags.doc: Wait for unit completion (vs return immediately).

flags.name: --on-active=TIME
flags.doc: Create timer that fires TIME after now.

flags.name: --no-block
flags.doc: Don't wait for command start confirmation.

examples.expected_output: transient scope created; backup runs with 4G mem cap
examples.scenario: Run a one-shot job under resource control.
Schedule an ad-hoc daily job without writing unit files.
Quick 'shell as user X' for testing.

purpose: Tree view of cgroups + processes within. Shows the slice/service hierarchy.

examples.scenario: See the cgroup layout of the running system.

purpose: Top-style live view of cgroup CPU/memory/IO/task counts. Real-time per-unit resource usage.

flags.name: -p, --order=path
flags.doc: Order: path | tasks | cpu | memory | io.

flags.name: --cpu={percentage|time}
flags.doc: CPU display: percentage of all CPUs or absolute time.

examples.scenario: See which service is consuming what.

purpose: Inspect + control logind sessions, users, seats. Where session data + suspend inhibitors live.

flags.name: lock-session [SESSION]
flags.doc: Lock a session (or current with no arg).

flags.name: enable-linger USER
flags.doc: Allow user services to keep running after logout.

examples.expected_output: SESSION UID USER SEAT TTY columns
examples.scenario: See who's logged in and how.

purpose: Query + extract core dumps captured by systemd-coredump.

flags.name: list [PATTERN]
flags.doc: List recent core dumps. PATTERN matches command name.

flags.name: info [MATCH]
flags.doc: Show details of a dump (signal, env, mounts, etc.).

flags.name: debug [MATCH]
flags.doc: Open core in gdb. Auto-fetches binary.

examples.expected_output: recent dumps: time, pid, uid, gid, sig, corefile-stored, exe
examples.scenario: See recent crashes.

examples.expected_output: gdb session on the dumped core
examples.scenario: Postmortem analysis.

purpose: Apply tmpfiles.d rules: create, clean (delete old per Age field), or remove specific paths.

flags.name: --boot
flags.doc: Apply 'F' / 'q' / 'Q' boot-only rules. Used by systemd-tmpfiles-setup.service.

flags.name: --prefix=PATH
flags.doc: Only apply rules whose path begins with PATH.

flags.name: --exclude-prefix=PATH
flags.doc: Skip rules whose path begins with PATH.

flags.name: --dry-run
flags.doc: Don't actually do anything; just print what would happen.

examples.scenario: Apply a new tmpfiles rule without rebooting.

examples.expected_output: old files deleted per Age fields
